meta.description: Performs structure-based virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, SMINA, GNINA (CNN scoring), and DiffDock-L hybrid workflows with explicit choice rules across rigid vs flexible docking, cross-docking vs self-docking, binding-site detection, receptor preparation, ligand preparation, and ultralarge-library screening.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 21 references in SKILL.md are real, verifiable papers (Trott & Olson 2010, Eberhardt 2021, McNutt 2021 GNINA, Buttenschoen 2024 PoseBusters, Lyu 2019 Nature ultralarge VS, Krivak & Hoksza 2018 P2Rank, etc.); no fabricated DOIs, trial results, or numeric claims found in any of the 7 test outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely computational hit-identification scope; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-facing claims in any output. Input 7 (adversarial 'give me one confident number, skip validation') was correctly handled without asserting docking scores as validated affinities.

methodological_ground.detail: SKILL.md repeatedly refuses false precision: 'must be calibrated for the target and library', 'there is no universal padding value', 'benchmark ... on target-relevant controls instead of assigning universal ... labels'. This discipline held up across all 7 test outputs; no methodological fallacy observed.

code_usability.detail: Ligand preparation, single- and multi-ligand Vina docking, and P2Rank pocket detection all ran unmodified except for a documented Windows platform substitution (CLI in place of the `vina` Python binding, which has no Windows wheel). Receptor preparation as literally written in SKILL.md failed for two confirmed, specific, fixable reasons (wrong script name; PQR parser crash on insertion-code residues) -- not treated as a full-skill FAIL because a working alternative exists within the skill's own materials and every other documented code path executed correctly. See P1 recommendations.

functional_suitability.note: Covers every promised use case (receptor/ligand prep, pocket detection, single dock, GNINA rescoring, hierarchical VS, ultralarge-library screening) with a well-matched, appropriately-scoped approach; docked 0.5 points for the two confirmed receptor-prep code defects (wrong script name, PQR insertion-code crash).

reliability.note: Ligand prep raises specific, typed exceptions at each failure point; the multi-ligand loop isolates per-ligand failures via try/except without aborting the whole screen (verified by inspection). Error messages are clear but carry no structured/parseable error codes.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 372 lines, entirely on-topic; usage-guide.md and examples/virtual_screen.py are correctly layered out of the main file.

agent_usability.note: Decision tables (docking-tool taxonomy, scenario tree, reconciliation matrix) sharply reduce ambiguity. Docked points because the primary documented Python-API pattern (`from vina import Vina`) silently assumes a working Windows wheel, which does not exist, forcing inference to reach the CLI fallback.

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md's example prompts ('Dock my compound library against this protein') match how a researcher actually asks. SMILES/embedding failures reject clearly (correct for Category 3, per the Scene Override) but offer no structured recovery hint beyond the exception text.

security.note: No credentials; subprocess calls use argument lists (no shell=True); user SMILES are parsed/validated through RDKit before any downstream use; no eval/exec of raw strings.

maintainability.note: Clean 3-way file split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/virtual_screen.py) and small composable functions. No example test cases or expected-output fixtures ship with the skill.

agent_specific.note: Precise, domain-specific trigger description; correct progressive disclosure; explicit, well-targeted cross-references to 9 related Skills with NotImplementedError stubs marking the hand-off points; strong escape hatches (covalent, metal-center, FEP redirects). Docked 1 point: no seed parameter/guidance for Vina, so pose ranks below #1 are not documented as reproducible.

key_strengths: Unusually rigorous methodological hedging throughout -- repeatedly tells the user to calibrate cutoffs, benchmark exhaustiveness on target-relevant controls, and verify pockets against orthogonal structural evidence rather than trusting a single score.

Binding-site detection and multi-ligand screening ran end-to-end without modification and reproduced real chemistry: P2Rank's top pocket matched the true benzamidine site (including catalytic Asp189) to within 0.6 A, and the docked amidine compounds correctly outranked non-binding decoys.
Extensive, specific failure-mode and reconciliation tables (per-tool failure modes, Vina-vs-GNINA disagreement matrix, common errors) that go well beyond generic troubleshooting advice.

Clean, purposeful cross-referencing to 9 related Skills with explicit NotImplementedError hand-off points, keeping this Skill's own scope focused on docking rather than sprawling into filtering/ADMET/pose-QC.

recommendations.title: 'mk_prepare_receptor.py' is not the installed command name
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's prepare_receptor() (line 76) and examples/virtual_screen.py's prepare_receptor() (line 42) both call subprocess with the literal command 'mk_prepare_receptor.py'. meeko 0.8.0 installs a console-script entry point named 'mk_prepare_receptor' (no .py suffix); the literal call raises FileNotFoundError.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented command name does not match the console-script name that pip actually installs for meeko 0.5+.
recommendations.fix: Change both call sites to 'mk_prepare_receptor' (or invoke the module directly for portability), and note in the Version Compatibility section that meeko's CLI entry points have no .py suffix once installed via pip.

recommendations.title: Documented --read_pqr receptor-prep route crashes on insertion-code residues
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's prepare_receptor() pipes pdb2pqr's default .pqr output into mk_prepare_receptor --read_pqr. On PDB 3PTB (trypsin, chymotrypsin numbering with insertion-code residues like '184A'), this raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '184A' inside meeko's PQR parser. Chymotrypsin-numbered serine proteases are a standard docking-benchmark family, not a synthetic edge case.
recommendations.root_cause: meeko 0.8.0's PQR reader assumes an all-integer residue-number column; pdb2pqr's PQR output does not pad/strip insertion codes into a format that parser accepts.
recommendations.fix: Switch the documented pipeline to `pdb2pqr --pdb-output <file>.pdb ...` followed by `mk_prepare_receptor --read_pdb <file>.pdb` -- verified working on the same structure in this audit, and already the pattern examples/virtual_screen.py uses (without showing how to produce the protonated PDB it expects). Unify the two receptor-prep code paths and add an insertion-code note to the Common Errors table.

recommendations.title: No seed/determinism guidance for Vina docking
recommendations.problem: dock_single() and virtual_screen() never set or expose a Vina seed. Top-1 affinity was empirically stable (-6.031, -6.020, -6.023 kcal/mol across 3 unseeded runs on the tested benchmark), but poses ranked 2+ reordered run to run, and SKILL.md never mentions --seed anywhere despite this skill's own emphasis elsewhere on reproducibility and recording run conditions.
recommendations.root_cause: The dock_single()/virtual_screen() function signatures omit a seed parameter, and no reproducibility guidance for the stochastic search step is given.
recommendations.fix: Add a seed parameter (e.g. default 42) to dock_single()/virtual_screen(), and one sentence recommending recording the seed for any screen whose top-N poses (not just the single best) will be reported or compared.

recommendations.title: 'from vina import Vina' has no Windows wheel
recommendations.problem: pip install vina fails to build on Windows ('Boost library location was not found'), so the primary documented Python-API code path in the 'Vina Docking (Single Ligand)' section and examples/virtual_screen.py cannot run at all on Windows; only the CLI works.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's existing CLI-fallback comment anticipates a Vina-*version* mismatch ('for Vina 1.1 use subprocess CLI') but not this platform-based one.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line platform note next to the existing version-based CLI-fallback comment: 'On Windows, pip install vina does not build a wheel; use the Vina CLI via subprocess instead.'

recommendations.title: Docked poses are not sanity-filtered before being returned
recommendations.problem: Vina's raw energies()/results.csv can include physically nonsensical outlier modes; a +68.69 kcal/mol pose appeared among 9 returned modes in testing here, which a downstream consumer could mistake for a real (if poor) binding estimate rather than a search artifact.
recommendations.root_cause: dock_single() and virtual_screen() return/report every mode Vina emits without a plausibility filter.
recommendations.fix: Note in the 'Vina Docking (Single Ligand)' section that positive-energy modes should be filtered or flagged before reporting, or clip n_poses reporting to affinity < 0.

recommendations.title: PDBQT-to-downstream-tool handoff is lossy for charged ligands
recommendations.problem: Converting a Vina/meeko PDBQT pose for a charged ligand (protonated amidinium) to SDF for PoseBusters -- the Skill's own cross-referenced QC step -- loses formal bond-order/charge information and fails RDKit sanitization, even though the pose's spatial placement (protein-ligand distance/overlap checks) is otherwise valid.
recommendations.root_cause: PDBQT does not encode formal bond orders; reconstructing them from atom types and distances during format conversion is unreliable for charged/aromatic-adjacent groups.
recommendations.fix: Note the PDBQT round-trip caveat in the pose-validation hand-off (Related Skills), or recommend carrying the original RDKit Mol (with correct formal charges) alongside the PDBQT rather than reconstructing bonds from docked coordinates alone.
